This person was released from Olomouc only by a provision of the Treaty of Campo Formio. Widely blamed for the massacre of the Champ de Mars as head of the National Guard, he later used the same position to assist in the March, 1830 revolution, This man alone signed the demand that king convoke the Estates General, but he lost his credit with the revolutionaries over support for the Monarchy a few years after writing the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen. Name this key figure in both the American and French revolutions.
Marie-Joseph-Paul-Yves-Roch-Gilbert du Motier, marquis de Lafayette

This person worked as a coordinator for the impeachment of James Peck and served as the U.S. Minister to Russia for two years. He drafted the Ostend Manifesto during his time in England, which led to his party's nomination. Before this, he had served as the chairman of the Committee on Foreign Relations and as Polk's Secretary of State. During the Presidential election, he defeated the first Republican presidential candidate as well as former president Millard Fillmore to win the election along with John Breckenridge. Identify this life-long bachelor, the fifteenth President of the U.S.

A contemporary account of this period is given in the Shih-chi of Ssu-ma Ch'ien. It is notable for the creation of the fu form and saw the introduction of Buddhism. Founded when Liu Pang overthrew Hsiang Yü, this dynasty was briefly interrupted by the Hsin when the rule of the child Emperor Ruzi was overthrown by Wang Mang. It is noted for Western and Eastern periods when the capitals were Ch'ang-an and Lo-yang, respectively. Name this Chinese dynasty lasting from 206 BCE to 220 CE.

A former leader of this entity was eventually captured by near Flensburg, where he had disguised himself as a farmer. The so-called third of them was known as Buna-Monowitz, and was built under Rudolph Höss. The site for all three was chosen for its proximity to a 44-track railway junction, above one track of which was hung a sign saying "Arbeit Macht Frei." name this military installation paired with an extermination center at Birkenau; the most notorious of the Nazi concentration camps.

In 404 AD, a monk of this name was stoned after he leapt into a gladiatorial arena, nudging Emperor Honorius to outlaw such games. In art, Jacques-Louis David painted this figure saying farewell to his young lover Eucharis. In mythology, this figure was banished to Cephalenia and married Circe, the mother of Telegonus. The first three books of a certain epic are sometimes named after this figure, who was received at Pylos by King Nestor three decades after Palamedes placed him in front of his father's plow. Name this Ithacan prince, a son of Penelope who longed for his father Odysseus' return.

This protégé of W.E. Channing persuaded Cyrus Butler to donate thirty thousand dollars to her cause. This woman studied the progressive York Retreat while recovering from depression at Greenbank, an estate in Liverpool owned by the Rathbone family. In 1842, she composed the pamphlet Memorial to the Legislature f Massachusetts, and later, was appointed Superintendent of Army Nurses. While teaching a class for female inmates, she observed troubled prisoners chained and lying in their own filth. Name this nurse and reformer whose efforts led to states erecting special hospitals for mental patients.

He avoided the Imperial service after a religious crisis at Trier, and this student of Aelius Donatus fled to Palestine after the death of his employer. While in Antioch, he experienced a vision in which Christ reproved him for his pagan studies. He praised virginity in the work Against Jovinian, and in his most important historical work, he wrote biographies of more than 130 Christian authors. However, this author of De Viris Illustribus is most remembered for a request made to him in 382 AD by Pope Damasus. Name this scholar who created the first Latin translation of the Bible, the Vulgate.

F. T. Frelinghuysen served as Secretary of State for this US President, who kept 80 pairs of pants in his wardrobe. His father was a co-founder of the New York Antislavery Society, and as a young lawyer, he won a landmark case leading to desegregation of public transport in New York City. This associate of Roscoe Conkling used tax money to reward political supporters after President Grant appointed him Collector of the Port of New York in 1871, and the Pendleton Act was passed 12 years later, during his presidency. Name this man who became president after James Garfield was shot.

In 2002, this nation won a dispute with a northern neighbor over the Bakassi Peninsula. This African country is home to the village of Rhumsiki, which many tourists visit to see Kapsiki Peak. This country's third largest city is Garoua, which lies on the Benue River, whose source is the Adamawa Plateau. This country shares its name with the highest peak on the West African coast, which is a thirteen thousand foot volcano. This country, which is sandwiched between Nigeria and Equatorial Guinea, lies to the west of the Central African Republic. Identify this West African nation whose capital is Yaounde.

This battle ended when a Chief of Intelligence found both the First and Second army headquarters in turmoil, and ordered a retreat towards Soissons. The original strike force was weakened when two army corps were diverted to the Eastern Front. General von Kluck was unnerved by the slow advance of the British Expeditionary Force into the gap which had opened between his left flank and von Bulow's right. Earlier, the first use of motorized infantry had occurred when a desperate General Maunoury was rescued by forces in taxicabs. Name this early battle of World War I on a namesake river.

This conflict was sparked by the execution of three men alleged to have been responsible for the death of John Sassamon. According to legend, a ghost led an unprepared militia to victory its decisive battle of Hadley. It was exacerbated by the murder of Wamsutta, which greatly angered his successor, the namesake of this war. Also precipitated by the deaths of treaty signers Massasoit and William Bradford, name this 1675-1676 conflict between New Englanders and the namesake leader of the Wamponoag Indians, also known as Metacom, who was nicknamed for his similarity to Alexander the Great's father.

Until recently, the known recorded history of these people consisted of a single document called the Edict of Telipinus. Their Indo-European language was referred to by native speakers as Nesite. After the turmoil caused by Sea Peoples, their empire disintegrated into city-states in their so-called "Neo" period. At their height, their empire spanned central Anatolia, northwestern Syria and upper Mesopotamia. Identify these people defeated by the forces of Rameses II at the Battle of Kadesh; foreign rulers of Egypt during the New Kingdom known for their chariots and iron weapons.

This election featured more vice-presidential candidates than presidential candidates, and Tom Watson won twenty-seven electoral votes for vice president despite being ignored by his running mate. Florence Kelley and Mary Lease notably campaigned for the eventual major-party loser, who did not earn his party's nomination until Altgeld transferred votes from Richard Bland. Henry Teller walked out of the Republicans' St. Louis convention over the main issue in this election, coinage. Identify this election famous for the "Cross of Gold" speech, the first time William Jennings Bryan lost to William McKinley.

This ruler influenced events after her through her sons Ochozias and Joram. A Sidonian princess, she had Naboth killed when he refused to sell his vineyard, after which Elias predicted the manner of her death, dogs. She attempted to ensure the supremacy of Astarte and Baal, whose worship she convinced her husband, Ahab, to allow. Identify this woman from the Books of Kings whose name has come to denote any scheming woman.

An important event in this country's history was the Christmas Uprising, which triggered a war that lasted for seven years. It was ruled for several centuries by elected Vladikas, or Bishops. An 1862 war with Turkey ended with its acceptance of terms offered by Omer Pasha-Latas, but it continued to fight until it was recognized as independent by the 1878 Berlin Congress. The only Allied country to be annexed by another country at the end of World War I, it remained part of that country even after the breakup of Yugoslavia. Name this newly independent nation that recently split from Serbia.

In 1905, this group excluded membership to anyone engaged in the sale of intoxicating liquors. Co-founders of it include William Ireland, John Trimble, and William Saunders. Officially known as the Order of Patrons of Husbandry, this group was founded by Freemason Oliver Kelley. It secured victory in the Supreme Court case Munn v. Illinois, which is known as one of its six namesake cases. Name this organization of farmers who fought railroad monopolies during the 1870's.

An attack on the 3rd Earl of Shaftesbury is found in his Alciphron, which was written during his time in Rhode Island. He also attacked the principles of calculus in a book entitled The Analyst. In 1713, this idealist wrote that material objects do not exist and that the universe is composed of minds and spirits. Name this Irish philosopher and adversary of Locke who believed "to be is to be perceived" and wrote Three Dialogues between Hylas and Philonous.

The Midland Counties Illuminator was a journal associated with this movement and was edited by Thomas Cooper. Member John Frost, attempted lead the failed Newport Uprising, nine years after which its last rally took place on Kennington Common. Members of it advocated moral force and demanded universal male suffrage, the secret ballot, and annual parliamentary elections. Name this movement begun by William Lovett, that was supported by workingmen in England in the 1840's and agitated for passage of the Six Acts of the People's Charter, its namesake document.

The year 1862 marked the first significant rediscovery of artifacts of this society, and in the 1920s, Frans Blom made the first descriptions of their cities. A recently discovered stone tablet known as the Cascajal block contains the mysterious hieroglyphs of this society. Their culture originated at San Lorenzo, but environmental changes caused a move to the city of La Venta, where many jade figurines were found showing half man, half jaguar creatures. Name this society that was located in central Mexico, which lasted from 1200 BC to 400 BC, and is mostly remembered for its large stone heads.

According to John Grigsby, this character's name refers to ergotized barley he consumed before battle. He once spent five straight days in icy water swam a whole day to reach the bottom of a lake that contains the abductor of Aeschere. Thanks to armor from Wayland, he receives eight horses for his two victories, the second of which was not thanks to a sword given to him by Unferth. The theft of a gem-covered goblet causes the ire of a dragon, who kills this Geat in battle, but not before he saves Hrothgar's mead hall. Name this Anglo-Saxon epic hero who slays Grendel and his mom.

This conflict saw Rainsborough take Prior Hill Fort during the siege of Bristol, while later, Manchester attacked Shaw House during the Second Battle of Newbury, leading to the Self-Denying Ordinance. The first battle in it saw a disputed victory for Henry Wilmot over the Earl of Essex at Edgehill, while subsequent engagements include a victory for Thomas Fairfax over Prince Rupert and Henry Ireton's use of cavalry in the New Model Army. Name this conflict that saw battles at Naseby and Marston Moor, in which Oliver Cromwell's Parliamentarians defeated Royalists of Charles I.

This conflict saw the last combat between fighter planes with piston engines fought and resulted in electoral success for the PCN, or National Conciliation Party. It was provoked by the eviction of squatting peasants who, it was feared, would return to their homeland and foment rebellion against rich landowners there. Lasting six days in July of 1969, it ended with a cease-fire brokered by the Organization of American States. Identify this war between Honduras and El Salvador given its name because it occurred soon after a series of FIFA qualifying matches.

This man hammered William Stanberry with his hickory cane, an action for which was defended a House trial by Francis Scott Key. The founder of the first school in Tennessee, this man received the Indian name Colleneh, "The Raven," from the Cherokee. Heavily wounded in the battle of Horseshoe Bend, he was later a representative from Nacogdoches to the 1833 convention at San Felipe. His most famous military exploit involved the 1836 victory over Santa Anna at San Jacinto. Identify this first president of the Republic of Texas and namesake of its largest city.

Some of them were threatened in the Meteor incident, but these were recovered. Among these items are 92 metopes. Part of the collection sat in a house on Park Lane upon their relocation, moving to a coal shed at Burlington House before being bought by the government. The outside row of their meropes depicts mythical battles, such as those between the Lapiths and centaurs. Also included is a frieze that displays a procession to a temple during a festival. Of the original 115 panels, only 94 remain, one of them housed by the Louvre. Name this collection of statues named for the man who moved them to Britain.

This person's father subdued the Kizilbash and defeated Ismail I at the battle of Chaldiran. This man himself was thwarted as Güns in a conflict that resulted from intrigues on behalf of János Zápolya. The employer of Khayr ad- Din, this ruler's forces slew Louis II at perhaps his most important victory, Mohacs. Name this son of Selim the Grim, an Ottoman Sultan known for both military and cultural brilliance.
Süleiman I, the Magnificent, of the Ottoman Empire

In Rastafarianism, this place name refers to a force in conflict with Jah, namely, the oppressive power structure of modern society. It names a version of the Talmud and, in the 137th Psalm, the Jewish people weep and remember Zion by the rivers of this city. Its earliest Biblical reference to it is in the book of Genesis, where its inhabitants, led by Nimrod, try to reach heaven, which results in God creating the different languages of the world. Name this ancient city on the banks of the Euphrates, the centre of an empire whose rulers included Nebuchadnezzar.

The surrender that ended this conflict was the subject of an 1899 painting by Lionel-Noel Royer. A notable history of this conflict was completed by Aulus Hirtius, who also wrote the history of the Alexandrine War, and these conflicts also saw Labienus and Publius Crassus in leadership positions. Ending with the after the siege of Alesia with surrender of Commius and Vercingetorix in 51 B.C.E, identify this series of conflicts, the subject of a notable "commentary" by the winning commander, Julius Caesar.

He worked with Mohammad Hatta, his future vice president, as head of BPUPKI, a Japanese organization that partially governed his nation. Nationalism, theism, social justice, internationalism, and representative democracy made up his Pancasila, or five pillars of governance. Named "President for Life" in the late 1950s, he was later deposed in a military coup in 1966 by the man who would replace him, and he died two years later. Name this father of Megawati and first president of Indonesia, the predecessor to Suharto.

After writing his Treatise on Probability, he contributed to the Cambridge cash-balance theory of money with his publication Tract on Monetary Reform, and responded to the Treaty of Versailles in his The Economic Consequences of the Peace. However, it was the work of Richard Kahn that resulted in his major idea, namely the multiplier effect arising from governmental spending. Name this British economist and author of The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money.

The chief god of the city of Babylon, he later became known as Bel, or Lord. Associated with the Sun, fertility and magic, he seems to have originally been an agriculture god since his symbol is a triangular spade. The son of Ea, his consort is Sarpanitu and he is often depicted with a scepter in his hand and a tunic decorated with stars. Identify this Babylonian god who slew the chaos dragon Tiamat to become the Lord of Heaven and Earth.

A mischievous child, he became renowned as a lover in his youth. His music would entice the gopis, or milkmaids, to leave their homes and dance with him in the forest. One story in the Puranas relates how using the ability of multiple presence, he was able to simultaneously satisfy hundreds of the milkmaids. Commonly depicted with dark blue skin and a crown of peacock feathers, his most important role came as advisor to Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita, where he explains the concepts of dharma and yoga. Identify this Hindu deity, the eighth avatar, or incarnation, of Vishnu.

This person led his father's forces at the battle of Evesham, ending the rebellion of Simon de Montfort. During his reign, the Jews were expelled, and Wales was brought under English control, with his heir born in Caernarfon Castle becoming the first to be titled "Prince of Wales." He in the Eighth and Ninth Crusades, but returned home after learning of the death of his father, Henry the Third. His tombstone refers to him as the "Hammer of the Scots" but in, the face of resistance from Robert the Bruce and William Wallace, he failed to conquer Scotland. Reigning from 1272 to 1307, name this king of England noted for his height.

The service that concludes this celebration is known as Ne'ilah and most wear white during it. Ritual slaughter of a rooster often occurs during this holiday. Originally instituted due to Leviticus 23:26, it is usually begun by the Kol Nidre. Beginning on the tenth day of Tishri, five days before Sukkot, it also includes the Amidah prayer, which expresses communal responsibility for sins committed previously. Not allowing work or consumption of food for 25 hours, name this "day of atonement," perhaps the most important Jewish holiday.

This man had five illegitimate children with his mistress Domitila de Castro, whom he eventually elevated to Marchioness of Santos, humiliating his first wife, Maria Leopoldina. He abdicated in favor of his daughter Maria II for his second throne, which he had received after the death of his father John VI. After he supported the revolt at Oporto, Andrada e Silva and his wife advised him to declare independence for his country, although he would later abdicate in favor of his five-year-old son. Name this ruler who, in 1822, became the first Emperor of an independent Brazil.

Liza Dalby wrote a fictionalized biography of this person who, in 1964, was designated by UNESCO as one of the world's greatest people. This author's father Tametako Fujiwara was an accomplished aristocratic poet, and a compilation of 128 of her own poems has appeared as her namesake collection, while her diary describes her time as an attendant of the empress Akiko. But she may be best known for a 54-chapter work about the love affairs of a certain prince of Japan. Name this eleventh-century author of The Tale of Genji.

This conflict arose in part from an attack on the plantation of Thomas Mathews, and its primary antagonists were cousins. It was organized in response to resolutions passed by the Long Assembly, which was later accused of corruption. Beginning with a "Declaration of the People," it eventually resulted in the hanging of 23 participants after attacks against friendly Native American tribes, the burning of Jamestown, and the death of its leader from body lice, much to the relief of Governor William Berkeley. Identify this 1676 revolt in colonial Virginia, named for the guy who led it.

It allowed merchants one year in event of war to continue trading merchandise in their home areas, and three commissioners would meet in Philadelphia to resolve disputes resulting from previously seized properties and cargo. Six months were given for the surveyors to meet at Natchez, to map the boundary called for by this treaty, which more importantly gave freedom of navigation of the Mississippi and the ability to deposit goods to the Americans. For ten points identify this treaty also known as the Treaty of San Lorenzo which set the southern border of the United States at 31degrees north latitude, negotiated by its namesake with Don Manuel de Godoy.

It initially attracted followers by the promise to share all property in common and its armies were divided into separate men and women's divisions. It was contemporaneous with the Nien Rebellion, which was put down after the defeat of this revolt. Frederick Townsend Ward and Charles Gordon, who commanded the Ever Victorious Army, were instrumental in suppressing this revolt led by a Hakka peasant named Hong Xiuquan (shiu-chuan), who claimed that he was the younger brother of Jesus Christ. Name this conflict during which the Qing Dynasty fought against the Heavenly Kingdom of Great Peace.

It was at it that St. Bridget was canonized, and its Frequens decree set up future councils. While the Spanish later got a say, at the start the five voting blocks were set up around Germany, Italy, France, and England. Much of its power came from the support of Sigismund and the Sacrosancta, but it took its namesake articles to overcome the flight of Baldassare Cossa, Antipope John XXIII. Identify this 15th century ecumenical council condemning Jerome of Prague and Jan Hus which dealt with the issue of having three popes by electing Martin V.

John Honeyman's reconnaissance mission was vital to the success of the victors in this battle, in which the losing commander had denied to his superior the need for building a redoubt. The attackers' southern column was led by John Sullivan, while Nathanael Green advanced from the north, and a third division that was to attack from the west never made it to the battle. American forces suffered minimal casualties, while capturing over 900 Hessians. Name this December 26, 1776 American Revolution battle in which George Washington coordinated a surprise attack by crossing the Delaware.

This person is the protector against the king of Seriphus for his mother, who has been banished from the realm of his grandfather, Acrisius. He had to bargain with Cepheus to wed his beloved, since she was destined to be sacrificed to a sea monster. He utilized the spoil of his best-known exploit to defeat Phineas; that exploit began as a fool's errand for Acrisius. Name this hero who enlisted the aid of the Graeae to slay the mortal Gorgon, Medusa.

One of the best sources on the art of this civilization is Alan Taube's commentary on the Dumbarton Oaks collection0 and definitive histories of these people were written by Michael Coe and Marshall Saville, who named them. A 1996 conference on them in Washington provided sculptural evidence that they believed their shamans transformed into jaguars, which they often depicted as hybridized with humans on the facades of their temples. Notable artifacts include large monuments at El Azuzul and a bird-shaped pitcher, though better- known are structures found around San Lorenzo. Name this civilization centered around La Venta, known for their huge stone heads.

One woman of this name married Alfonso XI and was beatified in a 1706 bull by Pope Clement XI. This was the monastic name of a student of Edmund Husserl who later died in Auschwitz, Edith Stein. It is given to two doctors of the church: one from Lisieux known for her "little way" of proving her love, and another who founded the Carmelite order. Give this name of the recently beatified founder of the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta, in whose context it is usually prefixed with Mother.

Fighting at this battle along Assunpink Creek saw the Knyphausen regiment surrounded, while the two major avenues in the town where this battle took place were King and Queen Streets. One commander in this battle wasn't awoken until the other side had captured an important redoubt; his name was Johann Rall. The highly trained professional soldiers on one side were hung over from Christmas partying and thus ineffectual. Name this Revolutionary War battle that saw Washington cross the Delaware and kick some drunken Hessian ass.

The Covode Committee chastised him for allowing the War and Navy Departments to award no-bid contracts, and late in his term he promoted his Postmaster General, Joseph Holt, to Secretary of War. Along with John Mason and Pierre Soule, this then ambassador of England was directed by William L. Marcy to explore the feasibility of purchasing Cuba via the Ostend Manifesto. He gained office thanks to the splintering of votes from Millard Fillmore on the Know Nothing ticket and John C. Fremont on the Republican ticket. Identify this bachelor president from Pennsylvania who saw seven states secede from the Union after his successor, Abraham Lincoln, was elected.

Despite the advantage of one side's Chassepot rifles in this conflict, that side got bogged down near the Saar River early in this war. Other engagements in this war saw the successive defeat of forces under Bazaine at the battles of Mars-la-Tour and Gravelotte. As a consequence of this conflict, the Papal States were annexed by Italy and Alsace-Lorraine also changed hands in the Treaty of Frankfurt. Prompted by the attempt to install Prince Leopold on the throne of Spain by Otto von Bismarck, it saw the decisive Battle of Sedan and led to the Paris Commune. Identify this conflict that saw the defeat of Napoleon III and the 2nd Empire.

This man rose to public prominence after successfully inciting his city- state to capture Salamis from Megara. After this man achieved power, he immediately returned seized land and freed all enslaved citizens, and during his rule, his city-state achieved the use of coins. After promulgating his laws on wooden tablets, this ruler left on a series of journeys. Directly after this man's death, his friend and general Pisistratus became tyrant of Athens. Identify this humane ruler of Athens who ended rule by aristocracy in favor of plutocracy by establishing the Council of 400 and ruled until 560 BC.

While aboard the Cassandra and the Walrus he acted as quartermaster alongside the gunner Israel. He trusts that his African wife will manage his estate during his absence from Bristol and his mobility is limited by an injury he sustained while in the service of Edward Hawke. He is responsible for the death of Arrow and after his schemes are revealed Abraham Gray is persuaded to leave him. He leads a mutiny against Trelawney and Smollet, the captain of the Hispaniola, and his nicknames are Barbecue and the Sea-Cook. This is what crutch-yielding pirate whose parrot's cries of "Pieces of eight! Pieces of eight!" end Stevenson's Treasure Island.

Mice lacking Cks2 were sterile because the gametes were unable to progress beyond this stage. Before this can begin, an E3 ubiquitin ligase must be activated which destroys the targets through the 26S proteasome. The degradation of one of those targets, securin, allows separase to breakdown cohesin, which marks the start of this. The cohesins hold together sister chromatids, and, once separated, daughter chromosomes are formed and move towards the spindle poles. Give the name of this stage of mitosis, which results in two sets of chromosomes being formed at the poles of the cell and that starts after metaphase.

Justice David Josiah Brewer was out of the country during this case, meaning only eight justices contributed to the final vote. Albion W. Tourgée and Samuel F. Phillips each helped prepare briefs for the plaintiff and were the only men to argue for him. William Rehnquist wrote a "Random Thought" supporting this decision two years prior to the 1954 case that would overturn it. John Marshall Harlan was the lone supporter of the plaintiff, who had previously lost his case against the State of Louisiana, which he claimed had denied him his Fourteenth amendment rights by jailing him for his refusal to sit in a colored train car. Name this 1896 Supreme Court case that upheld the doctrine of "separate but equal."

This event took its popular name from an event that saw only St. Abban the Hermit and Vortigern escape from a banquet crashed by a bunch of Saxons. The central target of this event was captured, given a pistol, and told to shoot himself, but refused and was shot point-blank by Michel Lippert. During its conception it was often referred to as "Operation Hummingbird" Those loyal to Franz von Papen were targeted, and the main objective was to end the independence of the SA under Ernst Röhm. Name this 1934 mass execution in which the Nazis killed at least 85 political opponents.

This city was formerly home to the Pruitt-Igoe housing projects that were torn down in the 1970s. Towns in a neighboring state that are across a river from this city include Venice and Brooklyn, while smaller rivers in and near this metropolis include Meremac and Des Peres. A suburb of this city contains a popular entertainment area known as the Delmar Loop. Forest Park sits in the west of this city, whose suburbs include Clayton, Florissant, and Ladue. Name this Midwestern city that is home to Washington University and the Gateway Arch.

This man was present, but not killed, during the explosion on the USS Princeton that killed Abel P. Upshur, and after his retirement he published an autobiography entitled Thirty Years View. Charles Lucas dueled this man on Bloody Island after accusing him of lying, and he was succeeded in his most famous post by Henry S. Geyer. He authored a series of Homestead Acts, and he gained his nickname after introducing a version of the Specie Circular into the Senate. He was almost shot by Henry Foote during a series of debates on the Compromise of 1850, and he supported his son-in-law John C. Fremont's expeditions to California. Also notable for attacking Andrew Jackson in a Nashville Hotel in 1813, name this nineteenth-century Missouri Senator nicknamed "Old Bullion".

One of this man's acts was to reverse a 1953 law that allowed abortion, and he also demolished the old legislature to replace it with the People's House as part of his "systematization" program. He established a list of banned books after reading books on Kim Il Sung's Juche idea; this was part of the fallout from a speech given in front of the executive committee that advocated a quasi-Maoist version of socialist realism, commonly called the July Theses. He originally came to power after the death of Gheorgiu-Dej, and is also notable for staying out of the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia. Nicknamed "Genius of the Carpathians", he was killed alongside his wife Elena on December 25, 1989 after a show trial. Name this final communist dictator of Romania.

This event led to a sermon given by John Allen at the Second Baptist Church in Boston that became popular pamphlet material. A man named John Brown was accused of being partly responsible for this action in an 1839 memoir by the last survivor of this incident, Ephraim Bowen. This was sparked when incensed townsfolk gathered at Sabin's tavern upon the arrival of Captain Lindsey and the Hannah and Namquid Point. A restaurant owner named Joseph Bucklin shot Captain Dudingston during this event, after which Abraham Whipple led a bunch of arsonists towards a schooner. Name this event in which some Rhode Islanders burned a vessel sent to enforce the Stamp Act.

Under this ruler's reign, the first printers in his country fled from his capital to Lithuania. This conqueror of Dorpat and Astrakhan gave up Narva in a treaty at Plussa with Sweden, and later renounced his claims on Livonia at the treaty of Jam Zaploski. He called the first Zemsky Sobor, and he had his private army of Oprichniks harass the boyars. His son Fyodor was succeeded by Boris Godunov, and he ordered the construction of St. Basil's Cathedral. Name this first Russian to take the title of Tsar, whose brutal treatment of Novgorod led to his nickname.

This man's half-brother led a revolt eventually put down by a bishop named Pedro de la Gasca, but managed to kill viceroy Blanco Nunez at the Battle of Anaquito. He joined up with a priest named Hernando de Luque and Diego de Almagro to search for gold near Darien. He led a band dubbed the "Famous 13" and gained over twenty tons of precious metals after setting up the "Ransom Room." He ambushed a leader at Cajamarca before strangling him and installing new head of state Manco Capac. Name this man who captured Atahualpa and conquered the Incan empire.

Polygnotus of Thasos and Hegias are among those thought to be this man's teacher. He supposedly depicted one of his students and eromenoi near the throne in one of his most famous work, a work funded by Delian League money. Another student, Agoracritos, was likely responsible for the statue of Nemesis at Rhamnus; that student also assisted this man on many of the Elgin Marbles. Identify this ancient Greek sculptor, the creator of the Athena Parthenos and the Olympian Zeus.

Fighting at Laodicea saw the annihilation of much of this movement's forces, which were meant to reinforce the armies of Joscelin II, and it was also routed at Dorylaeum. It spawned a companion Wendish campaign, and some of its members captured Lisbon. Eugenius III's papal bull Quantum praedecessores called this campaign, which failed to recapture Edessa and alienated former ally Damascus when it attacked that city. It was preached by St. Bernard of Clairveaux and led by Conrad III, Louis VII, and Eleanor of Aquitaine. Name this disastrous crusade that preceded the one led by Richard the Lionheart and followed the one called by Urban II at Clermont.

This is the name of an actor and associate of Mr. Wolf introduced by Tigg Montague to Jonas in Martin Chuzzlewit. It names the title character of a novel shortlisted for the 2007 Booker Prize that features Matilda, growing up during the Bougainville civil war, by Lloyd Jones. One character by this name is a shipkeeper pressed into service on Stubb's boat in Moby-Dick, while a Sherlock Holmes story name after five orange ones contains a murder by the Ku Klux Klan. Another character with this name befriends Herbert Pocket and tries to woo Estella, the foster-daughter of Miss Havisham.
